question: Can a purely geometric legal-move mask repair the eight known timeouts without changing any learned weights or successful routes?
cohort: All 22 non-exit starting cells, both fixed start times, all three saved seeds: 132 paired cases. Do not select only failures.
intervention: Evaluate the same saved position-only Q network once per cell. For the second variant set scores of moves without a neighboring traversable cell to -infinity before argmax. No hazard masks, cycle escape, revisit penalty modification, tie changes, epsilon or path heuristic.
tie_rule: First action index in the existing left/right/up/down order, matching torch argmax. An empty legal set is an error, not a silent fallback.
weights_policy: Load six completed models read-only with weights_only=True and eval/inference mode. No optimizer, gradients, replay updates or new training.
training_visit_audit: Only episode aggregate logs and final weights exist. Confirm the fixed reset state and saved log fields. Exact per-cell visitation and per-state/action replay counts are not reconstructable; never impute them from Q values.
harm_check: Report every original successful case whose masked action chain, FED or time changes, and every success-to-timeout pair. Do not interpret smaller dose on a timeout as successful evacuation.
diagnosis: Position-only fixed greedy action makes the policy a deterministic map of cell to next cell. Identify wall self-loops and legal cycles exactly; record Q values, selected actions and the first repeated-cell witness.
decision: Masking is an engineering execution variant, not proof of the authors' missing code. If masked timeouts remain, preserve them and close this mask-only round without another repair or additional training.
visibility: Eight original failures and all original scores are known. This is a posthoc development execution diagnostic, not an independent confirmation or generalization study.
scope: Same controlled synthetic FER as the previous method reimplementation; original FDS values, humans, crowds and new fire scenarios are not evaluated.
